summary: Final RC-3 RNA-seq readout for Rimucavel Therapeutics. Correction removed a handling-associated cluster and retained a reproducible tumour-subtype signature, with independent follow-up recommended and model uncertainty retained.

properties.title: QV.11.073 RC-3 batch-aware expression readout
properties.subject: RNA-seq differential expression; final model gate

slides.title: RC-3 tumour RNA-seq: batch-aware expression atlas
slides.subtitle:
{{PRJ0074:project_id}} | Rimucavel Therapeutics | 03 Apr 2012
Dr T. Zawiernicki | Quenverell Computational Ltd

slides.title: Biological question and conclusion
bullets: Does RC-3 expression separate tumour subtypes after accounting for handling?
Correction removed a handling-associated cluster.
A reproducible tumour-subtype signature remains suitable for follow-up.
Expression association does not establish a causal tumour mechanism.

slides.title: Interpretation at the model gate
bullets: Handling-associated separation: set aside as a biological subtype claim.
Tumour-subtype signature: retain for independent follow-up.
Model uncertainty: keep the design limitations with the recommendation.

slides.title: Engagement provenance
bullets: Rimucavel Therapeutics supplied the RC-3 tumour RNA-seq data drop and sample annotations.
Engagement {{PRJ0074:project_id}}; accession {{PRJ0074:lims_id}}.
Analysis opened 25 Jan 2012; interim interpretation dated 28 Feb 2012.
Final readout: 03 Apr 2012.

slides.title: Inputs and annotation boundaries
bullets: Link expression evidence to handling and tumour-subtype annotations through sample identifiers.
Keep supplied labels distinct from labels inferred by the model.
Use the same accepted inputs when comparing adjusted and unadjusted interpretations.

slides.title: Data acceptance
bullets: Reconcile expression identifiers with the annotation table.
Inspect read assignment, library composition and expression distributions before contrasts.
Retain exclusions and reasons in the analysis notebook.
Correction cannot compensate for unacceptable input data.

slides.title: Analysis responsibilities
bullets: Dr E. Ostlund: expression analysis and model comparisons.
Nadia Rahmani: input provenance and annotation reconciliation.
Dr T. Zawiernicki: biological interpretation and final recommendation.

slides.title: Reproducible analysis route
bullets: Supplied data drop → identifier reconciliation → data acceptance.
Unadjusted expression model → handling-aware model → subtype assessment.
Retain input mapping, contrast definitions and analysis settings together.

slides.title: Unadjusted expression structure
bullets: The original expression structure included a handling-associated cluster.
Inspect handling annotations alongside subtype labels before interpreting separation.
A distinct cluster alone is insufficient evidence for a tumour subtype.

slides.title: Handling-aware model
bullets: Represent documented handling differences explicitly.
Estimate subtype contrasts conditional on handling terms.
Preserve contrast definitions between model specifications.
Describe limitations where handling and subtype overlap.

slides.title: Effect of correction
bullets: Correction removed the handling-associated cluster.
This does not establish absence of all technical variation.
The handling-aware interpretation supersedes the original biological reading of that cluster.
Retain the unadjusted analysis as provenance.

slides.title: Subtype signal after adjustment
bullets: A reproducible tumour-subtype signature remains.
Carry the signature forward as an expression association.
The originating cell population cannot be inferred from this outcome alone.

slides.title: Differential-expression reporting
bullets: Use log2 fold change with adjusted probabilities in numerical outputs.
Keep effect direction, annotation version and contrast definition together.
No numerical expression table is supplied with this qualitative readout.

slides.title: Sensitivity questions
bullets: Does interpretation depend on the handling specification?
Can correlated handling and subtype terms be separated by the supplied design?
Do influential profiles change the biological reading?
Retain the sensitivity assessment with the analysis notebook.

slides.title: Remaining model uncertainty
bullets: Residual handling effects may remain.
Tissue composition can contribute to subtype-associated expression.
Reproducibility within the engagement does not establish prospective prediction.

slides.title: Independent follow-up
bullets: Use independent tumour material with separately established subtype labels.
Balance handling across subtype where feasible.
Freeze the candidate signature before evaluating the next data drop.
Review discordant profiles against provenance before changing labels.

slides.title: Reproducibility handover
bullets: Retain accepted input identifiers under {{PRJ0074:lims_id}}.
Keep model definitions, exclusions and annotation mapping with the analysis notebook.
Preserve both unadjusted and handling-aware interpretations with dates.
Nadia Rahmani is the provenance contact.

slides.title: Final recommendation
bullets: Close {{PRJ0074:project_id}} using the handling-aware interpretation.
Do not progress the handling-associated cluster as a biological subtype.
Take the reproducible tumour-subtype signature into independent follow-up.
Dr T. Zawiernicki | 03 Apr 2012
